text: Furthermore, Second Minister Tong outlined our moves to grow the capabilities of law firms and legal professionals – through adoption of LegalTech, facilitating access to overseas markets and uplifting all areas of the profession to grow new competencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Then, he spoke on Enforcement Mechanisms in Family Justice and Civil Enforcement; as well as helping the most vulnerable in our society access the legal system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: He also provided an update on the Community Disputes Management Framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Lastly, he announced our celebrations of the 200th anniversary of the establishment of Singapore's modern legal system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: I have covered SLA's efforts to optimise the use of state assets to meet changing needs and developments on the Digital Conveyancing Portal; our efforts to maintain a robust and balanced IP regime that supports creativity and innovation, as well as ensuring that the legal profession uses Gen AI safely and responsibly; new legislation to enhance protection for the vulnerable online; updates on the Protection from Harassment Court; implementation of reforms on personal bond; and leveraging technology for access to justice while preventing a digital divide.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Together, these form the foundations of our shared public life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
text: Laws are made together, and made legitimate, in this House, but it is only in the living and the working out of these rules, that we as a country, give them life.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: I have two sets of questions: one for Minister Edwin Tong, the other for Minister of State Murali Pillai.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: I truly welcome MinLaw's approach whereby they are looking to refining the debt repayment scheme, which is currently susceptible to abuse.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: I know of debtors who engage third-party consulting firms and they are charged exorbitantly for such services.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: And indeed, the debtors themselves are being asked to take up further loans to pay for such services.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: So, may I ask the Minister on the regulatory standpoint, how does MinLaw plan to enhance oversight of third-party debt consultancy firms to prevent misinformation and exploitation of debtors.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: And on the public front, whether the Ministry can consider collaborating with other Ministries or social service agencies to provide debtors with the accurate or reliable financial guidance and protect them from being exploited by such firms.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: For Minister of State Murali, on the digital office on the safety and online harms, the potential collaboration with MDDI.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: We note the challenges such that digital office may face to keep up with new technologies, high volume of harmful content and the misuse of anonymity.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: I understand that the Statutory Torts will be a whole suite that will be introduced by MinLaw, but would they also be pursuant to the double actionability rule for conflict of laws?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: For instance, does the Tort need to be actionable in Singapore and the country where that Tort occurred – the lex loci delicti and lex fori issues.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First, we will put information on MinLaw's website.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will enhance it, to make it informative and user friendly.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we will simplify as much as we can, as well as publish step-by-step guidelines, so that they can avoid going to these firms.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: And the jurisdiction is based on the civil jurisdiction of the Courts as it stands now, it is quite expansive.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: And in situations where the double actionability rule, which deals with the commission of Torts overseas, and whether or not there is a basis to pursue it here, whether it applies depends on the current rules.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I have two clarifications for Minister of State Murali on the Criminal Procedure Code amendments on pre-trial release.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And to this end, can he confirm that there are ongoing efforts to train, especially our law enforcement agencies, on the use of this new provision?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, just to follow up, I would just like to know whether there are ongoing efforts to train our officers involved on the new provision and how to apply it in applicable cases.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Certainly, we can convey the feedback as well.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If not, could I invite Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim to withdraw your amendment.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: With that, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.
